solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See the head of intelligence?

parts.note: wit is quick intelligence or cleverness
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A request to look at whoever runs a spy agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the head of intelligence' reads as a spymaster, but it is wordplay read backwards: the NESS (head) of WIT (intelligence).
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to observe it happening with your own eyes.

clue.text: Clown to wear motley in industrial dispute?

parts.note: a wag is a joker or clown

indicators.note: motley means mixed, so the letters of wear are jumbled

explanation.surface: A jester obliged to put on his patchwork costume during a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motley' makes EWAR from WEAR; 'motley' is also the jester's costume, which is the surface's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Read playfully, a fight over pay is a war about wages; the phrase means to fight a war.

clue.text: Winds on island, one in business

parts.note: the trades are the trade winds
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Breezes blowing on an island, where one person runs a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a shopkeeper or skilled worker, someone earning a living in commerce.

clue.text: Name for girl that would be otherwise without one

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for otherwise surrounds one

parts.note: else means otherwise
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl's name that would mean something different if one letter went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: ELSE goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a female first name, a pet form of Elizabeth.

clue.text: My boss is one that's crazy for inseparability

indicators.note: crazy indicates the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An employee complains that the boss is mad about togetherness.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbiosis is a close mutual dependence between two organisms or people, so they cannot be parted.

clue.text: W's vehicle had briefly seen teacher in action

indicators.note: in places the word for teacher inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
sir is how a pupil addresses a male teacher

explanation.surface: Something about a playwright's tram and a teacher glimpsed at work.
explanation.walkthrough: W is Tennessee Williams throughout: his play is A Streetcar Named Desire, so the vehicle 'had', shortened to 'd, makes DESIRE'D. 'seen' just joins the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The streetcar's name in the play title plus the contraction for 'had' spells the word.

clue.text: Dame's retreat at church

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: An elderly lady's hideaway at church.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Judi Dench is a celebrated British actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Judi Dench holds the title Dame, the female equivalent of a knighthood.

clue.text: Blind considerably reduced?

explanation.surface: A window shade cut down a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A SIGHT LESS, the second reading is the informal 'a sight less', meaning a lot less.
explanation.definitionFit: Sightless means unable to see; 'a sight' is slang for a lot, so 'sight less' is much less.

clue.text: Leader leaves country among sailors to return to track

indicators.note: among puts the shortened country between the letters for sailors

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: the first letter of the country departs

parts.note: Peru is a South American country

explanation.surface: A head of state leaves the country to rejoin the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader leaves' drops the first letter of the country; the Royal Navy supplies the sailors, a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To rerun a race is to go back to the track and run it again.

clue.text: Item of furniture behind the scenes

explanation.surface: A sideboard kept backstage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a theatre a dresser helps actors with costumes, working out of sight of the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a kitchen cupboard with shelves; it is also a theatre worker who looks after costumes backstage.

clue.text: W's endless sorrow about girl fellows get old pursuing

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word for sorrow wraps round everything else
endless means the word for sorrow loses its final letter

parts.note: grief is deep sorrow

indicators.note: pursuing means the men and ageing come after the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
men are fellows
to age is to get old

explanation.surface: A playwright's grief over a young woman as the men around her grow old.
explanation.walkthrough: W is Tennessee Williams throughout; this is his play The Glass Menagerie. 'endless' trims the last letter of the sorrow word, which 'about' wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Glass Menagerie is one of Tennessee Williams's best-known plays, so it is one of W's works.

clue.text: See 9
Using which Shakespeare's friend and queen turned white

parts.note: Mr W.H. is the mysterious dedicatee of Shakespeare's Sonnets
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

indicators.note: turned means the letters of white are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking by what means a Shakespearean friend and a queen went pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes EWITH from WHITE. The Sonnets were dedicated to 'Mr W.H.', so W.H. is Shakespeare's friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word means 'with which' or 'by means of which', so it is the same as 'using which'.

clue.text: Collector of clothes with name inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the letter for name goes within the word for clothes

parts.note: togs is informal for clothes

explanation.surface: Someone who collects garments, with a name tag sewn in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongs are a tool for gripping and picking things up, so they are a collector in a loose sense.

clue.text: Tough guy's male odour

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A remark that some hard man smells of a man.
explanation.walkthrough: BO stands for body odour.
explanation.definitionFit: The film hero played by Sylvester Stallone is the classic macho action man, a byword for a hard man.

clue.text: Stay the night the wrong way round and miss breakfast?

indicators.note: the wrong way round says the two halves of the phrase change places

parts.note: a sleepover is a night spent at someone else's home

explanation.surface: Spend the night at a friend's but somehow mix things up and miss the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: SLEEP and OVER swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping too long in the morning can make you late for the first meal of the day.

clue.text: Erect structure to go into body of W's vehicle

indicators.note: to go into says the rearranged letters are put inside the word for body

parts.note: a star is a heavenly body

indicators.note: structure as a verb means build in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Instructions for fitting an upright frame into the chassis of a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'structure' rearranges ERECT and 'to go into' sets it inside the heavenly body. W is Tennessee Williams: A Streetcar Named Desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetcar, the tram in the title of Williams's play, is the playwright's famous vehicle.

clue.text: Pointing inwards (in the case of one seeking to qualify)

parts.note: re is a formal word meaning concerning, in the case of
an entrant is someone entering a competition or exam

explanation.surface: A technical description of an inward angle, with a bracketed note about candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: A re-entrant angle points back into a shape rather than outwards.

clue.text: W's censor, not of Hair — not possible

parts.note: Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor and is known as Cato the Censor

indicators.note: possible here means the letters could form another arrangement, an anagram indicator

explanation.surface: A playwright's censor insists that the musical Hair cannot be staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' makes ONAHOTTINROOF from NOT OF HAIR NOT. W is Tennessee Williams: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof is a famous play by Tennessee Williams, so it is one of W's.

clue.text: State time and other directions for W

parts.note: E, N, N, E, S, S, E and E are compass points, i.e. directions

explanation.surface: Telling the time and giving further directions to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for W' adds that this is also the first name of Tennessee Williams, the playwright behind the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: See 17
Tree — situation, part of Alaska

explanation.surface: A tree, and where it stands, in America's northernmost state.
explanation.walkthrough: Sitka is a town in Alaska, and the Sitka spruce is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sitka spruce is a big conifer, and Sitka is also a place within Alaska.

clue.text: Competent about rebellion being within earshot

indicators.note: about means the word for competent surrounds the rebellion

parts.note: able means competent
UDI, Unilateral Declaration of Independence, was Rhodesia's 1965 break from Britain

explanation.surface: A capable person revolting where others can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: UDI was Rhodesia's 1965 Unilateral Declaration of Independence from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Audible means able to be heard, which is the same as being close enough to hear.

clue.text: City backed in dissemination

indicators.note: backed means the run of letters is read from right to left
in says the letters sit within the word dissemination

explanation.surface: A town that supported spreading information.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'dissemination' is SEMIN, which 'backed' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nîmes is a city in southern France, famous for its Roman arena.

clue.text: Chairman without companion is a tough guy

indicators.note: without means outside here, so the chairman goes round the companion

parts.note: Chairman Mao led communist China
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A party leader with no friends is a hard man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but means outside: the Chinese leader wraps the Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho as a noun is a man who makes a show of toughness and masculinity.

clue.text: End disheartened or end upset, being forced to abdicate

indicators.note: disheartened means the central letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: death is the end of life

indicators.note: upset means the letters of or end are scrambled

explanation.surface: Two ways to finish: losing heart or getting upset, as a monarch toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the heart of DEATH gives DETH; 'upset' makes RONED from OR END.
explanation.definitionFit: A dethroned king has been removed from the throne, i.e. forced out of office.

clue.text: Went out with old hat

explanation.surface: Courted someone in an unfashionable hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dated someone is to have gone on romantic outings; dated also means old-fashioned.

clue.text: Cider girl is back among eggs

indicators.note: among places the reversed word between the letters for eggs

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: back means is is read backwards

explanation.surface: A girl with cider is back among the eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cider with Rosie is Laurie Lee's memoir of an English village childhood; 'back' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is the girl of Laurie Lee's book Cider with Rosie.

clue.text: Musicians' gold box for the Sun

definitions.note: the clue's possessive 's is read as is: the musicians are

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a chest is a box
Ra was the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A band's golden chest intended for the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of instrumental players.

clue.text: Indian gentleman reinvented as Scots footballer

indicators.note: reinvented tells us the two letters of as swap places

parts.note: a Hib is a player for Hibernian, the Edinburgh football club known as the Hibs

explanation.surface: A colonial gentleman reborn as a footballer from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reinvented' turns AS into SA. Hibernian is an Edinburgh football club.
explanation.definitionFit: In colonial India the word was a respectful form of address for a European man.

clue.text: Robber to help with corn?

explanation.surface: A highwayman who also treats a sore toe.
explanation.walkthrough: A footpad was a highway robber on foot; a foot pad also cushions a corn on the toe.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpad was an old word for a thief who robbed travellers on foot, and a foot pad soothes a corn.

clue.text: W's medium has three Italian articles first

indicators.note: first means the articles come before the Italian number

parts.note: the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article
tre is Italian for three

explanation.surface: A playwright's art form begins with a trio of Italian grammatical words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three Italian articles' looks like three words from Italy; it is TRE (Italian three) after two English articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee Williams wrote for the stage, so drama for live performance was his medium.
